fixtureResults.description: PR that adds data transformation utilities using only real JavaScript/TypeScript built-in methods
AI-generated data transformation utility that calls Array.prototype.filterWhere() and String.prototype.replaceAllOccurrences() — neither method exists

actualFindings.message: Array.prototype.filterWhere() does not exist. `users` is typed as `ApiUser[]`, and `filterWhere` is not a method on JavaScript arrays (nor is it defined anywhere in this file or standard lib).
actualFindings.suggestion: Replace `users.filterWhere((u) => u.is_active)` with the standard `users.filter((u) => u.is_active)`.

actualFindings.message: String.prototype.replaceAllOccurrences() does not exist. `input` is typed as `string`, and `replaceAllOccurrences` is not a method on JavaScript strings.
actualFindings.suggestion: Replace `input.replaceAllOccurrences(',', ';')` with the standard `input.replaceAll(',', ';')` (ES2021+, widely supported) or `input.replace(/,/g, ';')` for broader compatibility.

fixtureResults.description: PR that adds a well-written data fetching hook with all real imports from existing packages
AI-generated metrics dashboard component that imports a non-existent Anthropic telemetry SDK and a non-existent named export from react-query

actualFindings.message: Package '@anthropic-ai/telemetry-sdk' does not exist on npm. Anthropic does not publish a telemetry SDK under this name.
actualFindings.suggestion: No direct replacement exists. Anthropic's real npm packages are '@anthropic-ai/sdk' (the core API client) and '@anthropic-ai/bedrock-sdk'. Cost/token metrics should be read from the API response objects (e.g. response.usage) and tracked with a real observability tool such as Datadog, OpenTelemetry, or a custom backend.

actualFindings.message: Named export 'useAutoRefresh' does not exist in '@tanstack/react-query'. This hook is not part of the library's public API in any published version.
actualFindings.suggestion: Use the built-in 'refetchInterval' option inside 'useQuery' instead: useQuery({ queryKey: ['metrics'], queryFn: fetchMetrics, refetchInterval: 30_000 }). This achieves the same auto-refresh behaviour without a fabricated hook.

fixtureResults.description: PR that adds a well-written test suite for a user authentication module with proper assertions throughout

actualFindings.message: Test 'throws for a malformed token string' uses `.rejects.toThrow()` with no argument, meaning it passes for any rejection — including accidental errors unrelated to malformed-token handling (e.g. TypeError, ReferenceError, network errors). It does not verify that the code throws the expected `TokenValidationError`, nor does it check the error message. Every other error-path test in this file passes a specific type or message to `toThrow()`, making this omission inconsistent and leaving the contract untested.

fixtureResults.description: AI-generated test file for a payment processing module. Tests look thorough but none make meaningful assertions — they only call functions and check toBeDefined() or toBeTruthy().

actualFindings.message: Test 'should handle the payment gateway response' is a mock-only test with a tautological assertion. The `spyOn` is set up on a local `gateway` instance that `processPayment` never uses (the module mock replaces the constructor globally), so the spy has no effect. The only assertion is `toBeTruthy()`, which passes for any non-falsy value and verifies nothing about the gateway interaction.
actualFindings.suggestion: Spy on `PaymentGateway.prototype.charge` (not a fresh local instance) and assert both the mock was called and the returned value matches the mocked response, e.g. `expect(PaymentGateway.prototype.charge).toHaveBeenCalledWith(mockPayload)` and `expect(result.id).toBe('ch_789')`.

actualFindings.message: Test 'should handle network errors gracefully' has zero assertions. The spy forces `charge` to reject, but `processPayment` is awaited with no `expect()` call. As the inline comment acknowledges, this always passes whether `processPayment` silently swallows the error, returns garbage, or re-throws (in which case the test would actually fail for the wrong reason).
actualFindings.suggestion: Add an assertion that reflects the intended contract: either `await expect(processPayment(mockPayload)).rejects.toThrow('Network error')` if errors should propagate, or assert on a specific error-state return value (e.g. `expect(result.status).toBe('failed')`) if errors are meant to be handled gracefully.

actualFindings.message: Test 'should process a valid payment' uses only `expect(result).toBeDefined()`, which passes for any non-undefined value — including `null`, `false`, `0`, or an empty object. It provides no meaningful verification of the payment result.
actualFindings.suggestion: Assert on specific fields of the result, e.g. `expect(result).toEqual({ id: expect.any(String), status: 'succeeded' })` or at minimum `expect(result.status).toBe('succeeded')`.

actualFindings.message: Test 'should return a result object' uses `expect(typeof result).toBe('object')`, which is a tautological assertion — it passes for any object, array, or `null` (since `typeof null === 'object'`). It does not verify any property of the returned value.
actualFindings.suggestion: Replace with a structural assertion such as `expect(result).toMatchObject({ id: expect.any(String), status: expect.any(String) })` to actually validate the shape of the returned object.
